supplementaryNotes.text:
Learning notes: Learn Trading in Nigeria

A localised free guide for Nigeria learners — local regulator, local exchange, tax note and the same $100,000 virtual practice account.

Published by TradeHQ, created by Anuga Weerasinghe. Publisher background and editorial approach. No independent professional review is claimed; any recorded source-check scope appears on the page.

Trading from Nigeria

TradeHQ provides a free paper-trading environment for people in Nigeria who want to build practical understanding of US and global markets without risking money.

Publisher and source-check scope

Published by TradeHQ; site creator: Anuga Weerasinghe. Regulatory source check: 2026-10-18. Linked regulator or registry information; no verification of individual eligibility, tax rates or remittance permission. No professional legal or financial review.

Why practise first

Paper trading lets users experiment with market mechanics using virtual cash without relying on a particular real-money platform, fee structure or FX-funding route.

How market access works here

For real-money market access, check the SEC Nigeria registered-operator database and the provider's current terms. The SEC also warns investors about unregistered online investment platforms, so verify registration rather than relying on marketing claims. TradeHQ itself does not require a brokerage account or payment.

Regulation

For securities regulation and intermediary information, consult Securities and Exchange Commission of Nigeria (SEC Nigeria). Registration for one activity does not establish that every product, overseas service or funding route is permitted. Use the official sources below for the applicable rules.

Broker types used locally
Capital-market operators in the SEC Nigeria registered-operator database — verify the current status of any provider before relying on it
Starting capital and eligibility

TradeHQ does not publish a real-money starting amount because provider minimums, fees, FX terms and personal circumstances vary. Verify current terms directly with a registered provider if you ever consider a real account.

Locally relevant assets to follow
The NGX All-Share Index as the domestic benchmark
USD/NGN as a currency-translation worksheet input, separate from a measured inflation effect
Brent crude, given the weight of oil in national revenue
US company reporting as study material, separate from eligibility to use an overseas provider
Country-specific practice worksheet

Optional study worksheet: model a fictional USD 100 oil receipt at two hypothetical NGN-per-USD rates. Next hold the rate fixed and change the dollar receipt. Compare currency translation with a change in export proceeds. Local inflation, production volumes, fiscal decisions and costs introduce further effects, so the worksheet cannot forecast the naira or a listed company. Keep a virtual stock-order exercise separate from any real account or funding decision.

Tax

Tax treatment depends on current law and individual circumstances. Check current official Nigerian guidance or a qualified tax professional; TradeHQ does not provide tax advice. This is general information, not tax advice — confirm your own position with a qualified local professional.

If you are a student

Students and beginners can use the simulator and courses to practise market concepts and document simulated decisions without risking money.

Questions people in this country ask
Is TradeHQ accessible from Nigeria? — Yes. TradeHQ is a global free website. No signup, no payment, no geo-restriction.
Can I trade NGX-listed stocks here? — Not yet. Current coverage focuses on US and global tickers.
References and related pages

SEC Nigeria — unregistered online investment schemes notice
All country guides
Beginner guide
Structured courses

Educational simulation only — not financial advice. Virtual money; no brokerage transactions. Quotes may be delayed, cached, unavailable or fixed simulator values; generated charts are labelled separately. Practice results do not predict investment outcomes.
